newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn urged to act early for smooth switch to Euro.
newsitem.headline: Bonn urged to act early for smooth switch to Euro.

text.p: Germany's bourse council on Tuesday called on the government to take swift action to ensure no business drains out of German financial markets once the Euro is launched as planned on January 1 1999.

The BSK council, made up of experts on bourse matters, issued a statement urging Bonn to pass framework laws to clarify the currency transition process, amid fears Germany could lose out to better-organised centres like France.

Share laws should be altered to make it possible for companies to issue shares without a par value in the transition period and existing benchmark Bunds should be converted into Euros at the earliest possible opportunity -- which is January 1 1999 -- the BSK insisted.
"Sales that have drifted off once are hard to win back, as experience has shown," the council warned.
The BSK is an advisory committee affiliated to both the German finance ministry and the Frankfurt stock exchange.
There was a particular danger that international bond investors could opt to invest in another EMU state if German Bunds looked unattractive at the transition time.
"It cannot reach a point where the market for benchmark bonds is split and Germany's financial centre suffers from reduced liquidity," the BSK said.

The German government has made no firm decision on the debt conversion issue, although it has said it is coming around to the idea of an early switch after other European countries including France announced firm plans to do so.
The BSK also called for a whole range of smaller legal amendments to allow a smooth transition to the Euro.

First, Bonn should impress upon corporate bond issuers that they do not need creditors' approval to convert their existing bonds to Euros, although it was up to the issuers themselves if and when they chose to make the switch.

Furthermore, the council sought alterations to securities pricing laws so that price changes involving just one (Euro) cent could be recognised, to eliminate the risk of "spikes" forming on price charts.
And regulations on trust holdings needed to be changed, the BSK said, to spare banks the huge expense of individually converting all their contents.
Finally, the BSK also said the bourse itself faced the challenge of reorganising its technical systems in preparation for the Euro launch.
The stock exchange should start discussions with banks and brokerages to determine how regulations on orders, pricing and settlement would have to be amended, the report said.
